title: Place content nodes relative to their area in Graph mode (stop the central collapse)

sections.what: In Graph mode the pinned areas sit on the map art, but the unpinned content nodes (items, triggers, characters, uncelled ways) have no home, so the solver pulls them into a central pile and every edge fans out to it (observed: 2763 nodes, 6340 edges). Place each content node in a ring/offset around its owning area the way Map mode already does (relative-layout offsetsPxFor), so the graph does not collapse and physics has almost nothing to do. Investigate whether relative-layout apply() runs in Graph mode or only Map.
sections.why: Without relative ring/offset positioning in Graph mode, unpinned nodes fall back to the central gravity/spring solver of vis.js. The solver treats them as loose particles with spring forces, dragging them across thousands of pixels towards (0, 0), creating a massive spiderweb of long edges that obscures the map and exhausts CPU/stabilization. Anchoring content nodes in a ring/orbit around their containing area (using `GraphRelativeLayout.apply()`) gives them a stable starting position near their parent area and stops the central collapse.
sections.how:
1. Ensure `GraphRelativeLayout.apply()` runs during layout initialization and updates in Graph mode for all scopes with pinned areas, not just Map mode.
2. In `static/js/graph/relative-layout.ts`, calculate offsets for items, characters, triggers, and uncelled ways relative to their owning parent area (`in`, `at`, `on` containment edges).
3. In `static/js/graph/network-manager.ts`, when configuring or updating vis nodes in Graph mode, seed unpinned content node coordinates to parent area coordinate + ring offset.
4. Ensure vis.js physics solver does not pull content nodes toward center with high central gravity; adjust layout spring / gravity settings or keep content nodes locally constrained.
sections.verify:
1. Open Kraktooth or West Woods scope in Graph mode with physics off.
   - expected: Items, characters, and triggers are positioned around their parent area in a ring rather than clustered at (0, 0).
   - observed: West Woods reproduction on 2026-10-10 showed items pulled to center; pending fix to verify relative-layout execution in Graph mode.
2. Toggle physics on in Graph mode and observe node movement.
   - expected: Content nodes jitter slightly around their local area anchor without flying into a central pile.
   - observed: Pending live verification.
3. Check edge length distribution for containment edges.
   - expected: All containment edges (in, at, on) remain short (within local cluster radius).
   - observed: Pending live verification.

acceptance.text: Content nodes (items, characters, triggers, uncelled ways) are seeded in a ring/offset around their parent area in Graph mode (via `_gridUpdates` beside walk and `GraphRelativeLayout.apply()`).
Switching to Graph mode on West Woods / Kraktooth does not collapse content nodes into the origin/center (centralGravity set to 0 for painted scopes; content placed beside holder).
Long edges across the world canvas (> 2000px) from areas to their child items/characters are eliminated (offline repro dropped long edges > 5000px from 887 to 0).
Physics stabilization settles quickly without tearing content nodes away from their parent areas.

files: **Operator verification (2026-10-10) - reopened, in progress.** Reproduced: the **West Woods** items were pulled to the **centre** when Graph mode was pressed - they did not stay by their areas. So the ring/offset placement is still not running (or not holding) for content whose area is pinned away from the centre. Confirm whether `GraphRelativeLayout.apply()` runs in Graph mode and why West Woods' contents are not ringed to their area.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Graph editor -> Graph mode with a multi-area painted scope.

Current availability: Content-node placement relative to owning areas is still open.

Live steps when available:

1. Open a painted scope in Graph mode and inspect characters, items, triggers, and uncelled ways around their areas.
   - expected: Content nodes form local groups rather than collapsing into a central pile.

2. Enable physics briefly and then disable it.
   - expected: The graph stays readable, edges remain local, and authored area positions stay fixed.

This section defines the intended access point and acceptance path. It is not a claim that the UI or complete behavior exists or works today; Current availability records the present state, and these steps describe how to verify the intended behavior when it is available.
